text: <h1>Why People Get So Excited About Sports<h1>
Ever wondered why people get so excited about sports? Whether it’s the World Cup, the Olympics, or a local match, millions tune in with passion. But why? The answer lies in psychology.

Humans love a good challenge. Watching teams or athletes compete gives us an ____ (strong feeling of excitement and energy), especially when the game is unpredictable. That last-minute goal or surprise victory keeps us ____ (very interested), just like a great movie or book.

Supporting a team makes us feel part of something bigger. Whether at a stadium or watching at home, ____ (supporting your team) together builds a strong emotional ____ (a connection between people). It's not just a game—it’s a shared experience.

We may not be pro athletes, but we feel their wins and losses as if they were our own. This emotional connection, called vicarious experience, explains why fans celebrate or ____ alongside their teams.
Sports offer a break from daily stress. For a few hours, we forget work or problems and just enjoy the game. It’s a great way to relax.
When our team wins, our brain releases dopamine. That excitement keeps us coming back, making sports more than just entertainment—it’s an emotional experience.
